attacks.claim: truncate() hard-cuts unbroken text at 280 code units when no whitespace exists and the text is the first token, so a long unparseable URL (toLink falls back to plain text) can be cut mid-URL. This contradicts the PR's 'a URL is never split' guarantee and the test name 'never splits a link or a word', whose last assertion expects a split word.
attacks.evidence: expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }]); and 'truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens'

attacks.claim: No wrapping rule is added for long URLs, and a leading link is always shown whole. On phones, an unbroken URL can overflow the description column, which is the mobile case this PR targets.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no overflow-wrap/word-break change for .item-description__body or the anchor; comment 'a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing'

attacks.claim: The ellipsis is appended after whatever was rendered last. That can produce 'see …' with a stray space, or attach '…' directly to a link's text, which makes it look like the URL itself was truncated.
Links open in a new tab with no visible or accessible indication. Screen-reader users get no warning that focus is moving to a new window.
attacks.evidence: {t.value}

attacks.claim: Neighbor-authored text becomes clickable, which makes it an easier phishing vector. The displayed text is raw Unicode, but href is the punycode-normalized url.href, so a lookalike domain can display one way and resolve another. The rel attributes do limit referrer and opener leakage.
attacks.evidence: const url = new URL(raw); ... return { kind: 'link', value: raw, href: url.href };

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT strips every trailing ')' and ']', so balanced URLs such as wiki-style links ending in ')' lose their closing paren and point to a different or broken URL.
There is no cap on description length. Tokenizing and rendering the full text on expand is unbounded, and the PR states no upper bound.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no max length on item.description or on rendered tokens; expanded branch renders all tokens

attacks.claim: Component state persists across items if ItemPage is not remounted on navigation, so a previously expanded description can stay expanded for a different item. Pure linkify tests also sit in the component test file.
attacks.evidence: const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false); (no key on ItemDescription); truncate/tokenize imported into ItemDescription.test.tsx
